examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Transmission delay is packet bits/rate; propagation delay is distance/propagation speed. Throughput of a long flow is limited by the bottleneck link, while latency adds relevant per-hop delays. The bandwidth-delay product counts data in flight; distinguish a one-way product from an RTT-based sender-window requirement.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A 20 Mbps link has one-way propagation delay 5 ms. How many data bits can be in flight on the link?

**Answer: 100000.** Bandwidth-delay product=20·10⁶ bits/s×0.005 s=100000 bits. An RTT-based continuous-send window would cover roughly twice this propagation amount plus any serialization convention.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Convert bytes to bits before dividing by a bit rate. Decimal network prefixes and binary memory prefixes can be different.

Mbps and MB/s differ by a factor of eight before prefix conventions are considered.
